key_insight: A minimal three-sphere model separates geometry- and friction-controlled particle trapping from fracture, with head-on collisions at larger size ratios requiring lower critical impact velocities.
engineering_relevance: The model can inform ball-milling impact conditions that favor particle capture and breakage rather than ejection.
method: Simulate three-sphere collisions using the discrete element method (DEM).
Describe trapping with a closed-form geometric condition accounting for friction.
Evaluate fracture from DEM output using Christensen-type stress and Weibull-type contact-force normalized criteria.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations link trapping and fracture outcomes to impact geometry and velocity, with fracture thresholds varying with impact angle, obliquity, and particle size ratio.
watch_item: The minimal three-sphere geometry may not capture collective interactions in a full mill, and the abstract reports no experimental validation.
paper_title: Trapping and Fracture of Particles in Three-Sphere Ball-Milling Collisions
